text:
ravi: Ran into a weird CI failure when trying to validate the quickstart in our Docker job. Installer ended up creating a directory named '~/.redwood' under the configured XDG_CONFIG_HOME instead of expanding the tilde. localtest couldn't load profiles and `redwoodctl auth login` failed with redirect_uri_mismatch. Anyone seen the tilde-not-expanded + redirect combo?

nina: ouch. is this GitHub Actions or your self-hosted runner? and what image?

ravi: GH Actions, ubuntu-latest image. job sets XDG_CONFIG_HOME=/work/.config to keep things in the workspace. install step was: `curl -fsSL https://.../install.sh | bash -s -- --prefix /opt/redwood` (noninteractive).

ops-bot: note: when running installers in containers that override HOME/XDG paths, avoid piping curl to sh in CI; but still worth fixing.

nina: can you paste `ls -la /work/.config` and the `redwoodctl --version`?

ravi: `redwoodctl 0.12.4`
ls output:```
/work/.config$ ls -la
drwxr-xr-x 3 1000 1000 4096 Mar 10 12:10 .
drwxr-xr-x 6 1000 1000 4096 Mar 10 11:58 ..
drwxr-xr-x 2 1000 1000 4096 Mar 10 12:09 '~/.redwood'
```

nina: definitely literal tilde folder. likely the installer wrote a template string `'~/.redwood'` into a config path without expanding $HOME or tilde. two fixes: move folder and chown, or re-run installer after fixing env.

ravi: moved and chowned, that unblocked profile discovery. but `redwoodctl auth login` opened the browser step in the job and got `400 redirect_uri_mismatch`. strange part: the installer-created client file had redirect uri `http://localhost:0/callback` (port 0). CI started localserve on 8081 for parallelism.

devex-bot: Known bug tracker: DX-1098 - installer sometimes writes redirect URI with port 0 when PORT env var is missing or incorrectly parsed. Workarounds: run localserve on 8080, or explicitly create a client with the correct redirect.

nina: thanks — that's different from the usual 8080 default. For CI you can create a client and point localserve at it. Example:```
# create a client with the proper port and replace installer file
redwoodctl auth create-client --name ci-local --redirect http://127.0.0.1:8081/callback > /work/.config/redwood/client.json
# or set REDWOOD_CLIENT_FILE to the new path before starting localserve
export REDWOOD_CLIENT_FILE=/work/.config/redwood/client.json
localserve --port 8081 &
```
Note: `auth create-client` will print secrets; treat them like secrets in the CI logs.

ravi: created client and swapped file, auth flow completed in the container. i'll open a PR to address both problems: (1) fix the installer template so it expands tilde and honors XDG_CONFIG_HOME/HOME even when run noninteractive or as root, (2) parse the port fallback properly so it doesn't default to 0, and (3) add a CI e2e that runs the tarball installer in a container with XDG_CONFIG_HOME set to a workspace path and verifies no directory names contain a literal tilde and that the saved client redirect uses a sane port (non-zero).

devex-bot: please reference DX-1098 in your PR and tag `devex/e2e` and `security` for client-secret handling in CI. Also add a small test that `redwoodctl auth create-client` can be used noninteractive and documented for CI use.

nina: when creating the PR, include the exact `ls` output and the minimal Dockerfile or job snippet to repro. i'll review the changesets for the installer templates. thanks for the clear repro. :thumbsup:

ravi: thanks — will send PR and ping for review.
